summary: Spawned a desktop substrate (engine 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001, rpc 42499) and rendered a bright green triangle (~25% coverage on an 800x600 blue-gray frame), then exercised capture_frame three ways. (1) save_path, no size args: inline block was the 768x576 default-ceiling image (768 long edge from 800x600, no upscale), while the saved artifact was full-res 800x600 / 5002 bytes (verified on disk) - full-resolution preserved independent of the downscaled inline. (2) scale 0.5 + max_dimension 256 + include_image: inline block 256x192 (800*0.5=400 then clamped to 256 long edge), composing in documented order. (3) not_all_black + no include_image: returned verdict NotAllBlack passed=true with NO image block - verdict-only default confirmed. Core surface works. Three friction points: geometry cannot be left persistently visible over the drive medium (retained-per-tick, cleared by the tick loop, no re-emitting component available), the mails-in-capture path is racy (same bundle gave blank then triangle), and the tool never reports the inline image block's own dimensions or encoded byte size in text.

artifact.rationale: The default inline PNG (768x576, downscaled from the native 800x600 frame) shows nothing but a flat, uniform slate-blue background — no recognisable shape whatsoever. A substrate-side check confirmed this objectively: differs_from_background passed=false ("no pixel in the scored region diverges from top-left (63,75,97)") and coverage fraction 0.0. The expected artifact requires that both the default and reduced PNGs visibly contain the same recognisable shape; the frame contains no shape at all, so the core visual subject the scaling behaviour was meant to demonstrate is absent. (The frame dimensions themselves are plausible — 800x600 native, 768 long-edge inline — but with an empty scene there is no shape to compare across scales.)

papercut.where: capture_frame mails bundle with retained-per-tick render geometry
papercut.what: The docs say mails are 'state changes that should appear in the image', dispatched atomically before readback. But the same DrawTriangle-in-mails bundle produced a BLANK frame on one call and the full green triangle on the next - nondeterministic from the caller's side. A single geometry submission accumulates into the next frame buffer and races the readback of the last recorded frame. Captures that also carried a checks reduction reliably showed the triangle (4/4) while a plain image capture missed once (1/2), so the outcome silently depends on which capture flavor is used.
papercut.suggested: capture_frame should commit/advance one frame after dispatching the mails bundle and before readback, so mail-staged geometry deterministically lands in the returned image; or, if that is intentional, document that retained-per-tick geometry submitted via mails is not guaranteed to appear and a persistent emitter is required.

papercut.where: capture_frame text output for a plain (no-checks) capture
papercut.what: A plain image capture with no checks and no save_path returns no text at all (capture 2 returned an empty text body); frame width/height appear only when a checks reduction is present. So the caller cannot even confirm the source frame dimensions on a plain capture. Inconsistent surface depending on whether checks were requested.
papercut.suggested: Always emit the source frame width/height (and, per the doc-gap above, the inline image dimensions/bytes) in capture_frame's text output regardless of whether checks were requested.

missing-primitive.where: Leaving a rendered frame visible for a later independent capture (the render-artifact 'leave it showing' contract) over the drive medium
missing-primitive.what: DrawTriangle geometry is retained-per-tick and is cleared by the live 60Hz tick loop within ~16ms; a plain re-capture after driving shows an empty blue-gray frame. The only persistence path is a wasm component that re-emits every tick, but the component registry is empty and the drive medium forbids authoring/uploading one. A pure-drive consumer literally cannot leave a static shape on screen for a judge to capture - it only appears when the DrawTriangle is passed in that same capture's mails bundle.
missing-primitive.suggested: Add a substrate primitive to pin/retain a static geometry batch across ticks (e.g. aether.render.set_persistent_geometry, or a 'hold last frame until cleared' flag), and/or ship a stock persistent-draw component (a triangle/mesh replayer) in the default registry so a drive-only consumer can produce a durable artifact.

doc-gap.where: Reporting each returned image block's dimensions and encoded byte size from capture_frame
doc-gap.what: The tool's text output never reports the inline image block's own width/height or encoded byte length. It returns the full-frame width/height only when checks run, and for save_path only the saved FULL-RES byte count - which cannot measure the scaled inline image. So the scaled inline PNG's dimensions and byte size (exactly what this task asked to report) are unobtainable through the public tool surface; a consumer would have to decode the returned image bytes themselves. The inline dimensions could only be inferred by re-deriving the 768-ceiling / scale / max_dimension math by hand.
doc-gap.suggested: Include the inline image block's width, height, and encoded byte length in capture_frame's text output (e.g. an 'image': {width, height, bytes} block) alongside the existing 'saved' block, so callers can compare inline vs saved without decoding pixels.
